questions.question: Explain why minerals are non-renewable and name three minerals and their uses.
questions.expected_answer: Minerals took millions of years to form in the Earth's crust, so once they are mined and used they cannot be replaced and can run out. Gold, which never rusts, is used for jewellery, wealth and electronics. Diamonds, the hardest natural substance, are used as gems and in cutting tools. Coal, formed from ancient plants, is burnt to make most of our electricity.

questions.question: Describe two ways mining affects the environment and two ways miners are protected.
questions.expected_answer: Acid mine drainage happens when old mines fill with water that becomes acidic and flows into rivers, and dust, smoke and gases from mines and power stations pollute the air. Mines also clear vegetation and make waste. Miners are protected by the Mine Health and Safety Act, which requires protective equipment, self-rescuers, refuge bays and training, and by their right to leave a dangerous place.

questions.question: Name the five stops on the heritage trail and what each teaches us.
questions.expected_answer: The Cradle of Humankind in Gauteng shows that humankind began in Africa. Mapungubwe in Limpopo shows a wealthy African kingdom with golden objects and Indian Ocean trade. The Castle of Good Hope in the Western Cape shows how meanings and identities change. The aloe in the Eastern Cape shows the value of indigenous knowledge of medicine. San rock art in the Drakensberg shows art linked to San beliefs that must be protected.
